description: The v0.6 corrections are NOT version-gated, while `allow_edit` is. A Hub that reversed this would keep accepting the exact broken asks v0.6 exists to stop — a sender has no reason to raise its declared minor for a correction it does not know about. Cross-cutting and behavioural; no single document can express it.
obligation: Submit each of these at `ma2h_version: "0.5"` (and repeat at "0.4" and "0.3"): (a) a `mode=input` ask with `schema: {"type":"string"}`; (b) a `select` whose `options` carry a duplicate `value`. The Hub MUST reject BOTH `422` at every declared minor, not only at 0.6 — §6 has fixed the input answer as an object and returned a bare `value` since v0.1, so neither ask was ever answerable or ever unambiguous under any version. A Hub that accepts them at 0.5 while rejecting them at 0.6 is non-conformant. Conversely `allow_edit` MUST be version-gated the other way: on an envelope declaring minor < 6, a Hub MUST IGNORE `permissions.allow_edit` (§10 robustness) and MUST still enforce `options[].value` membership at resolve (`422` for an off-menu value) — honoring it would grant semantics to a sender that does not claim to speak them, the defect §4 guards against for `to`. On an envelope declaring >= 0.6 the field is honored per dp-028. The distinction to preserve: a declared version scopes what a sender may ASK FOR, never what a Hub may refuse as malformed. FINALLY, the gate MUST be implemented where the Hub acts on the field, not by removing it from the envelope: submit an ask at 0.5 carrying `permissions.allow_edit: true`, then read it back — the stored envelope MUST still carry the field verbatim (§8.1 computes the dedup key over the submitted payload, so a byte-identical retry MUST recover the original ack rather than 409), and resolving it off-menu MUST still be refused 422. A Hub that strips the field instead passes the resolve half and fails the replay half, and additionally leaves every ask stored BEFORE it upgraded answerable off-menu — the stripping implementation can never reach those.
